skill.description: Automate Outlook Calendar workflows through Rube MCP, including event creation, search, updates, deletion, invitations, and meeting-time discovery.
skill.summary: Guide Outlook Calendar scheduling, search, updates, and meeting-time discovery through Rube MCP.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most static external command and blocker findings are false positives from Markdown backticks, tool names, and parameter examples in SKILL.md. The hardcoded Rube MCP URL is a real network dependency, and the skill requires delegated Outlook Calendar access through a third-party MCP service. No prompt injection or data-exfiltration intent was found in the reviewed file.

remediation.suggestion: Document the Rube and Composio data flow, required Microsoft OAuth scopes, and token revocation steps before marketplace publication.

remediation.issue: Calendar actions can notify attendees or delete events
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before create, update, delete, decline, or invitation-sending actions.
Explain why rube.app/mcp is required and advise users to verify the endpoint in their client configuration.

static_findings.snippet: - Active Outlook connection via `RUBE_MANAGE_CONNECTIONS` with toolkit `outlook`
- Always call `RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS` first to get current tool schemas
**Get Rube MCP**: Add `https://rube.app/mcp` as an MCP server in your client configuration. No API k
1. Verify Rube MCP is available by confirming `RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS` responds
- `end_datetime`: ISO 8601 end time (must be after start)
- `time_zone`: IANA or Windows timezone (e.g., 'America/New_York', 'Pacific Standard Time')
- `attendees_info`: Array of email strings or attendee objects
- `is_html`: Set true if body contains HTML
- `is_online_meeting`: Set true for Teams meeting link
1. `OUTLOOK_GET_MAILBOX_SETTINGS` - Get user timezone for accurate queries [Prerequisite]
3. `OUTLOOK_GET_EVENT` - Get full details for a specific event [Optional]
4. `OUTLOOK_GET_CALENDAR_VIEW` - Get events active during a time window [Alternative]
- `start_datetime`/`end_datetime`: For CALENDAR_VIEW time window (UTC with Z suffix)
- `attendees`: Updated attendee list (replaces existing if provided)
- `body`: Updated description with contentType and content
- `send_notifications`: Send cancellation notices to attendees (default true)
- `attendees`: Array of attendee objects with email and type
- `meetingDuration`: ISO 8601 duration (e.g., 'PT1H' for 1 hour, 'PT30M' for 30 min)
- `StartTime`/`EndTime`: Time window for schedule lookup (max 62 days)
**Get Rube MCP**: Add `https://rube.app/mcp` as an MCP server in your client configuration. No API k
- time_zone is required and must be a valid IANA or Windows timezone name
- user_id defaults to 'me'; use email or UUID for other users' calendars
- event_id is required; obtain from LIST_EVENTS first
- Valid filter fields: start/dateTime, end/dateTime, subject, categories, isAllDay

content.value_statement: Coordinating Outlook meetings is slow when calendars, attendees, and Teams links must stay aligned. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Rube MCP Outlook workflows.
actual_capabilities: Create Outlook events with subjects, times, locations, attendees, descriptions, and optional Teams links.
List, search, and retrieve calendar events using Outlook filters, calendar views, and selected fields.
Update event details after resolving the correct event identifier.
Delete events or decline invitations with notification controls.
Find available meeting times and free or busy schedules for attendees.
Resolve mailbox timezone settings before time-sensitive calendar queries.
limitations: Requires a connected Rube MCP server and an active Outlook OAuth connection.
Can send invitations, updates, or cancellations when calendar actions are executed.
Does not bypass Outlook permissions or delegated calendar access limits.
Tool schemas may change, so the skill instructs agents to search tools first.

use_cases.title: Schedule Team Meetings
use_cases.description: Create Outlook events with attendees, locations, descriptions, and optional Teams meeting links.

use_cases.title: Find Calendar Availability
use_cases.description: Search calendars and compare attendee availability before proposing meeting times.

use_cases.title: Maintain Meeting Records
use_cases.description: Update, delete, or decline calendar events after identifying the correct Outlook event.

prompt_templates.title: Create A Meeting
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Outlook Calendar Automation to schedule a 30-minute planning meeting tomorrow at 10:00 AM. Include the attendees I provide and create a Teams link.

prompt_templates.title: Search My Calendar
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Outlook Calendar Automation to find my events next week that mention project review. Show the date, time, subject, and attendees.

prompt_templates.title: Reschedule An Event
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Outlook Calendar Automation to find the customer sync this Friday, confirm the event, then move it to Monday afternoon with the same attendees.

prompt_templates.title: Find Group Availability
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Outlook Calendar Automation to check availability for five attendees over the next two weeks and suggest three one-hour meeting slots during business hours.

output_examples.input: Schedule a project kickoff for Tuesday at 2:00 PM with three attendees and a Teams link.
output_examples.output: Created the Outlook event for Tuesday at 2:00 PM, added the requested attendees, and enabled a Teams meeting link.

output_examples.input: What is on my calendar tomorrow morning?
output: 9:00 AM: Product standup with the product team.

output_examples.input: Find a one-hour slot for the launch team next week.
output_examples.output: Found three available options next week and ranked them by attendee availability. Ask before creating the final event.

best_practices: Confirm the target calendar, timezone, attendees, and notification behavior before changing events.
Search for the current Rube MCP tool schemas before selecting Outlook tools.
Use narrow date ranges and selected fields when searching large calendars.
anti_patterns: Do not create, update, delete, or decline meetings without clear user confirmation.
Do not assume the user timezone when mailbox settings are available.
Do not replace attendee lists unless the full intended list is known.

faq.question: What does this skill automate?
faq.answer: It guides Outlook Calendar workflows for creating, finding, updating, deleting, declining, and scheduling meetings through Rube MCP.

faq.question: Do I need Rube MCP?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill requires Rube MCP and an active Outlook connection before calendar workflows can run.

faq.question: Can it create Teams meetings?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains the required Outlook event settings for creating Teams meeting links.

faq.question: Will it email attendees?
faq.answer: It can trigger invitations, updates, cancellations, or decline responses when the selected Outlook action sends notifications.

faq.question: Can it manage shared calendars?
faq.answer: Only when the connected Outlook account has the required calendar permissions or delegation.

faq.question: How should I reduce risk?
faq.answer: Confirm the calendar, attendees, timezone, event identity, and notification settings before executing any calendar change.
